summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would take money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to run the Parliamentary Departments for part of the 2016-2017 financial year.
It would provide about five-twelfths of the estimated annual funding for those departments, excluding new budget measures.
The remaining seven-twelfths of the annual funding, plus full-year budget measures, would be covered by a separate bill to be passed later.
changes: The bill appropriates money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for Parliamentary Departments.
It funds the first part of the 2016-2017 financial year.
It allows the next Parliament to pass a similar bill for the rest of the year if needed.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: The Supply Bill (No. 1) 2016-2017 seeks $35 billion in appropriations for interim government funding from 1 July 2016, covering ordinary annual services until November 2016, with special provision for the Australian Electoral Commission.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: The Supply Bill (No. 2) 2016-2017 seeks approval for just over $6 billion in appropriations from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for non-ordinary annual services, including capital works and payments to states, territories, and local governments, to ensure funding continuity from 1 July 2016. It also sets debit limits for the Nation-building Funds, the Building Australia Fund, the Education Investment Fund, and general purpose financial assistance and national partnership payments.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: The Supply (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2016-2017 was moved to provide interim funding of just over $97 million for the Department of the Senate, Department of the House of Representatives, Department of Parliamentary Services, and the Parliamentary Budget Office, covering parliamentary expenditure from 1 July 2016 until approximately the end of November 2016.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: The Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2016-2017 seeks just over $147 million for the operations of the Department of the Senate, the Department of the House of Representatives, the Department of Parliamentary Services, and the Parliamentary Budget Office, including over $25 million for Parliament House maintenance.
